title: Scripturequest Price Gate
subject: Constitutional Law
stem:
Ruth’s Workshop, Inc., a private company founded by Ruth, makes ScriptureQuest, a Bible-trivia board game sold through ordinary retail stores around the country. A state allows board-game makers to sell games in the state only if each month they certify that the price charged for the same game in every other state during that month is not lower than the in-state price. The state insists that it is regulating only sales inside its borders.

What is the company’s strongest dormant Commerce Clause objection?
call: What is the company's strongest dormant Commerce Clause objection?

choices.A: The law is valid because price rules never affect commerce.
choices.B: Article IV privileges and immunities is the only relevant doctrine.
choices.C: The law directly controls prices charged in other states and risks impermissible extraterritorial regulation.
choices.D: The law is valid because a state may control all nationwide prices once a seller enters its market.

rightExplanation:
C is correct. The statute does not merely set the price for sales inside the state. It makes access to the in-state market depend on what the seller charges in every other state during the same month.

Gold Key: A state may not condition in-state sales on a seller’s out-of-state prices. When the in-state sales gate is tied to prices charged elsewhere, the strongest dormant Commerce Clause objection is extraterritorial price control.

Silver Key: Follow the pricing lever, not the state’s label. The state says “inside our borders,” but the certification forces the seller to account for prices outside the state.

c3.label: CUT A
c3.text: “Price rules never affect commerce” is a tiered absolute. Prices are the commercial object in the stem.

c3.label: CUT B
c3.text: Article IV privileges and immunities is a doctrine-home misfit. The call asks for a DCC objection.

c3.label: CUT D
c3.text: The answer stretches a true-sounding in-state-market rule into power over all nationwide prices. That is an extreme-of-range overclaim.

c3.label: RESIDUAL C
c3.text: It matches the price lever in the stem: in-state access depends on out-of-state prices.

c3.label: CLASH
c3.text: No two-answer clash remains after the cuts.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: The residual is confirmed by the Gold Key.

studentScript: Call says DCC. Cut Article IV. Cut price-rules-never. Cut all-nationwide-prices as overreach. The only answer that follows the price lever across state lines is C.

A.signal: The word 'never' overclaims; the stem is about prices, which are commercial.
A.lawyer: Price regulation is regulation of commerce; this answer cannot support validity.

B.signal: The call says dormant Commerce Clause; this answer exits into a different doctrine.
B.lawyer: Article IV privileges and immunities is not the only relevant doctrine; the operative objection is DCC price control.

C.signal: This answer tracks the stem's lever: sell here only if prices elsewhere meet the state's condition.
C.lawyer: Price-affirmation statutes tying in-state sales to out-of-state prices fall within the Baldwin / Brown-Forman / Healy line.

D.signal: The true kernel is local sales power; the bad move is stretching it to all nationwide prices.
D.lawyer: A state may regulate in-state sales but may not control prices charged wholly outside the state.

goldKeys.statement: A state may not condition in-state sales on a seller’s prices charged wholly outside the state. Price-affirmation laws tying in-state access to out-of-state prices are classic dormant Commerce Clause danger zones.
goldKeys.trigger: in-state sales permission depends on prices in other states
authority: Brown-Forman Distillers Corp. v. New York State Liquor Authority
National Pork Producers Council v. Ross

silverKeys.statement: Ignore the state’s label and follow the lever. If the in-state sales gate moves when out-of-state prices move, the DCC objection is extraterritorial control.
silverKeys.trigger: certify prices in every other state
silverKeys.unlocks: state says it regulates only inside its borders

remediation.title: Price Gate Across State Lines
remediation.signal: Sell here only if prices elsewhere satisfy this state’s rule.
remediation.studentMove: Follow the price lever across the border.
remediation.tinyRule: In-state access tied to out-of-state prices points to DCC extraterritorial price control.
